title: Reference-guided procedural elephant and LTC area-light proof
objective: Create an editable static elephant from the owner's ep02_elephant_ref_r7.png as visual guidance, using local procedural modeling without Trellis2, and verify Blender plus separate Harness V4 previews with researched LTC area-light integration.
forbidden_paths: existing episode sources and accepted masters
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the owner's reference identity and record visible invariants plus inferred hidden anatomy; do not claim a scan or exact reconstruction.

Actual editable Blender model shows connected elephant masses, four plausible weight-bearing legs, broad fan ears, long curved trunk, two ivory tusks, small eyes, nails, tail and detailed matte skin; no placeholder primitive assembly is presented as final.
Add a bounded static elephant recipe to the local MCP contract; preserve existing recipe behavior and unsupported rig/animation/physics rejection.
Export self-contained GLB and verify actual reimport topology, bounds, semantic IDs and materials; budget below one million evaluated triangles.
Render four actual Blender views and obtain independent reference-based criticism; patch identified defects with repeatable evidence.
Research the supplied LTC paper using primary sources; apply actual RectAreaLight/LTC support in isolated V4 proof and distinguish shading from shadowing.
Verify the actual Windows MCP build and native V4 still output; preserve a source archive for the previously accepted v0.1 implementation.
Persist current task, provenance, source/evidence hashes, limitations, documentation and a local opener; human approval of the new elephant remains separate.
verification: Strict schema tests including elephant parameter limits and legacy fixture acceptance.
Real official SDK stdio build and image retrieval on Windows.
Blender export/reimport and multi-view visual review.
Separate V4 render with actual installed dependencies, image visibility and repeat-frame checks.
Independent code/asset review and source-bound evidence.
human_gates: The user's current instruction authorizes creating the elephant and local lighting experiment.
Human acceptance applies to final appearance; do not infer it from approval of the previous prop scene.
No paid generation, GitHub push, publishing, episode migration or schedule changes.
risks: Single view does not determine hidden anatomy or exact physical dimensions.
Procedural skin can differ from reference; actual images must be inspected.
LTC area-light shading does not itself establish area-light shadows.
The added recipe changes implementation hashes; preserve the old runtime source for historical evidence.
notes: User explicitly reserves Trellis2 for their own selected cases; use the image for visual direction only.
